newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares extend losses in late trade. [CORRECTED 17:01 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German shares extend losses in late trade. [CORRECTED 17:01 GMT]

text.p: German shares extended their losses in late trade on Friday as traders took profits ahead of the weekend and amid concerns about a possible U.S. interest rate hike next month.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index dropped 1.1 percent, or 38.92 points to end the day at 3,357.57 points, drifting down from its bourse trade close of 3,374.10 points.
The main event of a lacklustre afternoon was a technical blip that disrupted price displays in late trade, giving values on the DAX several thousand points ahead of the real value.

Market interest focused on the construction sector after builders Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG, in favour after both said they were pulling out of Germany's high-speed rail Transrapid project because of questions about the project's costs.

"It's a money pit project and the market so far thinks it is good for the construction groups to get out now," said one trader. "But there's still speculation they may return to the project in some form in the future."
Holzmann shares ended IBIS trade up four marks at 480 marks while Hochtief rose 1.14 marks, or 1.8 percent, to 64.50 marks.

Shares in steel group Thyssen AG, which said the controversial project would go forward, dropped 7.45 marks to 375.95 marks while Siemens AG, another remaining partner, was down 35 pfennigs at 90.10 marks.
Few other shares attracted interest as the market generally focused on the Wall Street drop and prospects for a rate hike in May on remarks by Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer.
"The dollar is still buoyant but Meyer's suggestions for another rate hike are dampening enthusiasm," a trader said.
